newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Bid talk reignites British power stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bid talk reignites British power stocks.

text.p: Shares in Britain's remaining independent electricity suppliers surged in heavy trade on Wednesday, powered by renewed bid rumours and talk of further consolidation in the sector.
East Midlands Electricity Plc led the group, jumping 52 pence to 589.5p in late trade and topping the London stock market's percentage gainers on the back of bid rumours.
"There's a lot of bid speculation around the stock, although no names have been mentioned," one dealer said, echoing others.

Speculation surrounding Britain's regional electricity companies (RECs) heated up last week after a unit of U.S.-based CalEnergy launched a hostile 650 million pound ($1.07 billion) bid for Northern Electric Plc.

Northern Electric, which is due to release sparkling half year results early in an attempt to attract a higher bid, saw its shares fall a penny to 631.5p in late trade after posting sharp gains since last week.
But Britain's four other independent RECs shot higher.
Besides East Midlands, Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc's shares rose 15.5 pence to 754, while Southern Electric Plc jumped 21.5 pence to 669, and London Electricity Plc gained 12 to 617.5.

Analysts said the bid for Northern Electric -- the second for the company in nearly two years -- had highlighted interest in the RECs, particularly from U.S. firms looking to move into Britain and bypass profit regulation at home.
PowerGen Plc's attack on Britain's industry's regulator also helped fuel takeover speculation, dealers said.

Ed Wallis the chairman of PowerGen, Britain's second biggest generator, criticised the Office of Electricity Regulation (Offer) on Wednesday for promoting an industry which he said was crowded with firms unable to survive as effective competitors.

"I am not sure that is really the best way of introducing competition because these players do not have the skills and the weight...to survive as effective players in the market in the longer-term," Wallis told Parliament's Trade and Industry Committee earlier on Wednesday.

PowerGen's own attempts to move into the electricity supply sector by buying Midlands Electricity were blocked seven months ago in a surprise government decision. Since then it has been accused by some analysts of not offering investors an alternative strategy.
Analysts believe U.S. firms are keen to buy regional electricity companies ahead of the next British general election, due by May 1997, at which the opposition Labour Party could win power.
Labour has criticised previous takeovers and may take a more protectionist line with foreign companies attempting to take over the country's utilities.
Seven of Britain's cash-rich RECs have already been sold -- including three to U.S. utilities.
